fixes.explanation: Good guess, friend, but the song doesn't hand the credit to an army. The singers talk straight to the LORD: “O LORD, You will establish peace for us. For all that we have accomplished, You have done for us.” Notice they don't say He helped a little. They say what they accomplished, He did, so even their peace and their wins go back to Him. An army would be taking a bow at that point, and this song has nobody taking a bow but the LORD.

Nice thought, friend, but the song doesn't bring up their fathers. It sets up a contrast: “…other lords besides You have ruled over us, but Your name alone do we confess.” The line is about who sat over them and who they still stand with. I think that's the point of the word "alone," because it leaves no room for anybody else's name on the list. Whoever was in charge, only one name gets confessed, and it's the LORD's.
